Description

RAS proteins signal from more than one membrane. Live probes showed that endogenous RAS is activated by mitogens on the Golgi apparatus, and that HRAS and NRAS engage RAF1 there, so RAS on different membranes reaches different pathways [1]. On the Golgi the exchange factor is RASGRP1. When Src activates phospholipase Cγ1, RASGRP1 moves to the Golgi and activates RAS there. The same second messenger, Ca2+, switches RAS off at the plasma membrane through the GTPase-activating protein CAPRI (RASA4) [2]. Which membranes a RAS isoform visits depends on its C-terminal anchor. HRAS and NRAS are palmitoylated: they lose and regain their palmitate in a cycle that traps them on the Golgi and returns them to the plasma membrane through the secretory pathway [3, 4]. KRAS4B carries a polybasic stretch instead, which sends it straight to the plasma membrane [4, 5].

References
